name: Ceinsys Tech Ltd
title: Ceinsys Tech Ltd - 538734 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q1 FY27 revenue flat at INR158 crore (+1% YoY) with margin up to 24.4%; order book INR990 crore but management refused all forward guidance and UBR/cash conversion remains weak (164-day working capital cycle).

summary.headline: Ceinsys Q1 FY27 revenue flat at INR158 crore (+1% YoY) but EBITDA rose 27% to INR39 crore, margin 24.4%; order book INR990 crore.
summary.overview: Consolidated operating revenue was INR158 crore, up about 1% YoY, while EBITDA grew 27% to INR39 crore and margin expanded 505 bps to 24.4%. PAT was INR31 crore, a marginal decline, with PAT margin at 19.6% (down about 59 bps). Order inflow was INR143 crore against about INR157 crore executed, lifting the order book to INR990 crore from INR880 crore. Management withheld forward guidance throughout, citing policy, and focused on receivables recovery (JJM dues), a proposed AI cloud JV, and undeployed funds from the earlier fundraise.

financial_highlights.change: up from INR880 crore in Q4 FY26
broadly flat vs prior two quarters (162-164 days)

segments.name: Geospatial Engineering Services
segments.commentary: Revenue INR94 crore, up 30% YoY; majority of the INR143 crore fresh order inflow came from geospatial enterprise solutions. Management said the mix shifts with project execution phase.

segments.name: Technology Solutions
segments.commentary: Revenue INR63 crore, down about 25% YoY. Management aims to take this segment beyond 51% of segment revenue.

segments.name: Mobility (incl. international subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Mobility is now a division after the Allygrow merger; management reported improving order book and a top-line increase and margin improvement at the US subsidiary. Mobility is run-rate and not built into the order book.

guidance_outlook: No forward guidance given on revenue, margins or order inflow, citing company policy.
Management said growth should show in the next 2-3 quarters as orders with 3-6 month execution convert, and expects to sustain the growth trend seen over the last 2.5 years.
Management said it is on track with order book milestones and believes margins of around 22-23% are achievable, citing the 24.4% in Q1.
Management expects a better operating cash flow in FY27 than in FY26, without quantifying it.
Expected collection of about INR100 crore of JJM/IoT dues by end of Q3 FY27, with overdues expected to be cleared before 31 March 2027 per the Maharashtra GR.
Management expects one large national-program order (similar to the earlier INR350-400 crore L1 opportunities) possibly in FY27 Q4 or Q1 FY28, and said two L1 positions were pending award.
capex_capacity: Board approved up to INR25 crore investment in a 50:50 JV with AI Fabric USA for a sovereign AI cloud (GPU-as-a-service, model-as-a-service, AI services); first tranche INR5 crore for incorporation, second INR20 crore after due diligence.
JV incorporation expected in about 1-1.5 months; due diligence (technical, market) to take 3-4 months; business model to be frozen after that, with commercial activity indicated for FY28.
Management said it is evaluating acquisitions, aiming for vertical integration and margin-accretive deals; no deal announced. Acquisition multiples cited at 5-10x EBITDA.
Around INR230 crore raised earlier, of which INR130 crore received in March 2026 and INR100 crore in September 2024 (per management clarification).
demand_pricing: Order book INR990 crore; execution timelines range from 3 to 18 months, with some O&M contracts running 2-5 years. Weighted average execution 12-18 months.

Run-rate businesses (mobility, OEM products and services) sit outside the order book; about INR50 crore of Q1 revenue came from these. Management estimated 20-25% of FY26 revenue (of INR660 crore) was outside the order book.

Key Q1/recent wins: INR67 crore Madhya Pradesh PMAY manpower/LoI (over 3 years); INR17 crore Bhandara Municipal Council AMRUT 2.0 smart water meters (12 months); INR4 crore EKS InTec order; INR4 crore US subsidiary order; INR30 crore aggregate T Second purchase orders.

Management said JJM-related bids are being deprioritised in favour of transport (ITMS/ATMS), energy and other geospatial opportunities where budgets are funded. Transport positive developments expected in 1-2 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the execution timeline of the INR990 crore order book and the funnel outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Execution spans 3 to 18 months, with O&M extending to 5 years; weighted average 12-18 months. Management said the funnel is strong and it will not give a numeric funnel figure or guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why does the order book roll-forward not match inflow minus revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said run-rate businesses (about INR50 crore of Q1 revenue) are not booked in the order book. Net order book increased about INR110 crore after INR157 crore of execution. Reconciliation to be sent via the IR agency.

qa_highlights.question: What is the AI cloud JV economics and will Ceinsys be an EPC player?
qa_highlights.answer: The JV is 50:50 with AI Fabric USA, targeting defence and government sovereign cloud. Management said it intends to be an AI solutions company, not EPC, with contractors used for construction.

qa_highlights.question: What are the receivables and JJM dues outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital cycle at 164 days, flat. About INR100 crore of IoT/JJM dues expected by end of Q3 FY27, per the Maharashtra GR. Management said billing is being collected with no new build-up.

qa_highlights.question: Are large orders (INR350-400 crore L1 positions) likely by Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: INR67 crore order already received. Two more in process, with one possibly in Q2. Management declined to commit on timing but said tender pipeline remains strong, and a large national program order could come in 1-2 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why not a share buyback given idle funds and low valuation?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said buybacks are funded from surplus operating cash, and the raised funds are for growth. Management said it would not invest only to deploy capital; acquisitions must preserve margins.

qa_highlights.question: Why is unbilled revenue high and when will it convert?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the large unbilled revenue (about INR320 crore at 31 March, per the analyst) is mainly JJM; it is expected to be billed and reduce over the next 2 quarters as government funds come in.

risks_watch: Order book roll-forward: management said net order book rose about INR110 crore after INR157 crore execution, but analysts' arithmetic on INR140-143 crore inflow vs INR148-157 crore execution did not tie; reconciliation promised via IR agency.

JJM/IoT receivables: about INR100 crore expected by end Q3 FY27 and overdues targeted before 31 March 2027; unbilled revenue (about INR320 crore per analyst) and working capital cycle of 164 days need to fall for cash conversion to improve.
Large-order conversion: two L1 positions (INR350-400 crore class) pending award with timing not committed; management said it would not give timing or guidance.
Revenue growth: Q1 revenue flat YoY and Technology Solutions down about 25%; management declined to guide FY27 turnover despite claiming growth will show in next 2-3 quarters.

AI cloud JV with AI Fabric USA: INR25 crore commitment (INR5 crore first tranche, INR20 crore after due diligence); business model not frozen until after 3-4 months of due diligence, commercial activity indicated for FY28; capital deployment of idle funds and acquisition plans remain undefined.
key_quotes: We don't give the forward guidance because that's not within our policy.
So, next 2 quarters looks very upbeat and -- as in last concall also, we said that we have a robust funnel.
We don't intend to be an EPC company. We intend to be the AI solutions company. That's the objective.
And this unbilled revenue will automatically go down in next 2 quarters once we have this funds from the JJM projects.

We don't want to invest just for the sake of investing we want to see that investments are in line with what we are doing either it is vertical integration backward or vertical integration forward within our line of business so that it enables the margin expansion.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on margins (24.4%) and order-book momentum but cautious and repeatedly evasive on quantified guidance, citing company policy, on order timing, funnel size, FY27 turnover, and acquisition plans. Answers on the order-book reconciliation, unbilled revenue and cash flow were more direct, while the buyback and valuation questions drew defensive responses.
